t: 7.3 Class question: are the charts globally accepted?
p: Part 7: Summary and Closing Questions
x: Q: Are these charts, data and scale measurements globally accepted? A: Yes. After thorough research, the course's R&D team included the ones that are well known, well accepted and verified. They are not all from one country: the research comes from the United States and other places, including parts of Europe, so it is a mixed global contribution.

These are places where the recording was unclear, inconsistent, or differs from the slides or the E-book. The lecture's version is kept in the notes. Please check each against your course material. DEXA accuracy. The lecture says DEXA has "good accuracy compared to the gold standard". The slide says it is "as accurate as hydrostatic weighing". The E-book says it is considered "more accurate and valid than a two component model such as underwater weighing" because it accounts for bone mineral. These wordings differ. DEXA advantages list. The slide lists five advantages (low radiation, no special clothing, no special preparation, available widely in India, as accurate as hydrostatic weighing) and one disadvantage (may be expensive for some). The board lists more (time saving, no technical expertise needed, suitable for all, in-depth analysis). The notes follow the board and the recording. Cost of a DEXA test. About 3,000 to 4,000 at a government facility and 12,000 to 15,000 at a premium hospital: the currency was not stated (taken as rupees) and the figures are approximate. Entry-level versus high-end BIA (class question). The recording is garbled here (it also mentions a figure of "45 lakh" for a machine). The notes say that entry-level BIA gives a combined fat figure and high-end BIA can split subcutaneous and visceral fat. Please confirm. Beginner rule. The question at the start is worded as "Muscular endurance. Will this test be conducted for beginners?", but the explanation and the retest rule are about muscular strength. The notes apply it to strength. The E-book agrees that strength testing is not prescribed for people starting out. Whether the same rule applies to muscular endurance tests is not stated. Rockport case study arithmetic. Recomputing the male case gives 43.781, while the slide prints 43.79 (the female case, 15.985, matches). The category (Very good) is unchanged. The female case was only on the slide. Rockport norms table. In the age 65 male row the Excellent range prints as 48-42 (the pattern suggests 46-42), and in the age 65 female row Poor is printed as 23-20 and Very poor as below 20. Both the slides and the E-book print it this way. The table also lists only certain ages (15, 20, 25 and so on); the lecture did not say how to treat ages in between. Rockport pace and pulse. The lecture and slide say "as fast as possible"; the E-book says a brisk pace, almost as fast as possible without breaking into a jog, and states an error range of 5.0 ml O2 per kg per minute. The 10-second pulse x 6 matches the E-book. The recording says the Rockport test was created by an institute located in Rockport in the United States; this was not checked. Step test details. The lecture, slide and E-book agree on the 12 inch board, 96 bpm, 3 minutes and 1-minute pulse. The E-book describes one cycle as 4 beats (up, up, down, down), which the lecture also taught. The count of 24 cycles a minute (72 in 3 minutes) is derived by the notes, not stated. Strength norms categories and cases. The slides group the percentiles into five categories (90 and 80 well above average, and so on). The E-book labels only 90, 70, 50, 30 and 10. The leg press case (twice body weight, 2.00) lies between the 80th (1.93) and 90th (2.07) percentile, which the slide puts in well above average. The numbers 124/100 and 200/100 were hypothetical examples. The women's bench press 60+ column (0.64 at the 90th percentile) is higher than the 50-59 column (0.61) in both the slides and the E-book. Curl-up protocol. The lecture and slides: tape distance 12 cm (under 45) or 8 cm (over 45), metronome 40 bpm, repetitions till failure, norms with values up to 75. The E-book describes a partial curl-up test: tapes 10 cm apart, metronome 50 bpm (25 curl-ups per minute), one minute, a maximum of 25 repetitions, with different norms. The age limit was said once as "younger than 40" in the video explanation, while the rule is under or over 45. An age of exactly 45 is not

Course: Personal Training Certification Topic: Fitness Testing, part 2 of 2 (hydrostatic weighing and DEXA, then the cardiorespiratory, muscular strength, muscular endurance and flexibility tests) About these notes: Short revision version of the Fitness Testing 2 lecture. For the full explanation of every concept, example and class question, see the Detailed Notes. Sources: the lecture recording, the course slides ("Fitness Testing 1 & 2"), the course E-book chapter on health screening and evaluation, and the board photos. Big idea: A fitness test is only worth using when it is valid, reliable, available and carried out in a standardised way. For body composition, DEXA wins among the eight tests because it gives a body fat percentage, an in-depth three-category analysis and is available in India. For the other components, each test fixes the conditions (height, speed, range of motion, posture) so that one result can be looked up in a norms chart for the client's gender and age.

Archimedes principle applied to fat and muscle It is a densitometry method: body density = mass / volume. Underwater weight is read on a scale connected to a seat, and volume comes from the water displaced. Body density goes into the Siri equation to give body fat percentage. Archimedes part 1: volume of the object underwater = volume of water displaced. Part 2: water displaced = buoyant force (the upward push). Point | Fat | Muscle | 1 Volume | More | Less | 2 Water displaced | More | Less | 3 Buoyant force | Higher | Lower | 4 Density compared with water | Lighter than water | Heavier than water | Result | Tends to float | Tends to sink | Points 1 to 3 follow Archimedes. Point 4 is a property of the tissues, not Archimedes. Procedure: water at neck level, blow out all the air (air also makes a person float), stay still, read when the bubbles stop, and repeat several trials. Gold standard: highest accuracy, and other tests are compared against it. Disadvantages: needs technical expertise, expensive, not available to the public and not available in India.

DEXA principle Dual Energy X-ray Absorptiometry (spelling: absorptiometry). Two beams, one high energy and one low energy, are sent into the body. The denser the tissue, the more it absorbs. Tissue | Density | Absorption | Bone | High | Very good | Muscle | Moderate | Some absorbed, some passes | Fat | Low | Poor | It reports three categories: fat-free mass (muscle, organs, fluid), fat mass (subcutaneous, visceral and essential fat) and bone and mineral mass. Originally used in orthopaedics to check bone density, now used for overall body composition. Advantages: low radiation risk, no special clothing or preparation, good accuracy, quick, no technical expertise needed for the user, suitable for all, available in India, in-depth analysis. Disadvantage: might be expensive for some (about 3,000 to 4,000 at a public facility, 12,000 to 15,000 at a premium hospital). Gym BIA machine: compare it with a DEXA reading (about plus or minus 5 percent) and repeat DEXA after about 6 months.

t: 4.1 Rockport 1 mile walking test (sub-maximal VO2 max)
x: Walk 1 mile (1.6 km) as fast as possible, non-stop. Four inputs: time (minutes), pulse, age, weight in pounds (kg x 2.2). Pulse: counted for 10 seconds x 6, immediately at the end, because the peak heart rate is needed. Sex | Formula (weight in lbs, time in min, pulse in bpm) | Female | 132.85 - 0.388 x age - 0.077 x weight - 3.265 x time - 0.156 x pulse | Male | 139.168 - 0.388 x age - 0.077 x weight - 3.265 x time - 0.156 x pulse | Worked case (male): age 50, 60 kg (132 lbs), 15 minutes, pulse 108. Subtract 19.400 + 10.164 + 48.975 + 16.848 = 95.387 from 139.168 to get 43.781 (the slide prints 43.79). In the age 50 male row, 44-40 is Very good. Slide case (female): age 38, 140 lbs, 21 minutes, pulse 146 gives 15.985, Very poor. Rows used in the cases (VO2 max, ml/kg/min): Age | Sex | Superior | Excellent | Very good | Good | Fair | Poor | Very poor | 30 | M | 54+ | 53-49 | 48-44 | 43-39 | 38-34 | 33-29 | <29 | 30 | F | 51+ | 50-46 | 45-41 | 40-36 | 35-31 | 30-26 | <26 | 50 | M | 50+ | 49-45 | 44-40 | 39-35 | 34-30 | 29-25 | <25 | 50 | F | 47+ | 46-42 | 41-37 | 36-32 | 31-27 | 26-22 | <22 |

t: 4.2 YMCA 3 minute step test (heart rate recovery)
x: Step test and curl-up metronome beats Standardised conditions: board 12 inches, metronome 96 bpm, 3 minutes non-stop. One beat = one move: up, up, down, down. Then the client sits and the pulse is counted for one full minute (recovery is the aim, so not 10 seconds x 6). Case: female, 30 years, 85 bpm: below 88 in the 26-35 column, so Excellent. Lower is better. Rating | Female 26-35 years | Excellent | < 88 | Good | 88-99 | Above average | 100-111 | Average | 112-119 | Below average | 120-126 | Poor | 127-138 | Very poor | > 138 | | Rockport walk | YMCA step test | Aim | Peak heart rate for VO2 max | Recovery of the heart | Pulse count | 10 s x 6, at once | Full minute after the test | Metronome | None | 96 bpm |

Strength tests Muscular strength is the force produced in one maximum effort, so the load is the 1 RM. Relative strength (strength ratio) = weight lifted / body weight. Absolute strength is just the weight lifted. Tests: bench press (upper body) and leg press (lower body). The leg press is supported and does not depend on the core, unlike the squat. Cases (male, 30 years): bench press 1.24 (for example 124 / 100) and leg press 2.00 are both Well above average. Beginners: skip strength at the first test. The second test counts as the first strength test and the third test begins tracking progress.

Both tests are done till failure (no target number). | Push-up test | Curl-up test | Region | Upper body | Abdominal region (rectus abdominis, spine flexion) | Position | Males on toes, females on knees | Supine, palms flat on the mat | Range of motion | Chin to the floor, arms fully extended, no half repetitions | Fingertips travel from tape A to the far tape: 12 cm if under 45, 8 cm if over 45 (inside edge to inside edge, tape 2 cm wide) | Speed | Not set | Metronome 40 bpm, 2 beats = 1 repetition | Cases | Male 30 reps: Excellent. Female 27 reps: Excellent | Male 25 reps: Below average. Female 25 reps: Average | Curl-up tape set up A repetition does not count if the palm lifts off the mat. The chart is separate for males and females, so each client is compared like with like.

Flexibility tests overview Flexibility is the ability of the muscle to lengthen passively (the trainer helps), so both sides are tested. Goniometer: measures joint angle (fixed arm, moving arm, central point on the joint). Only a physiotherapist or orthopaedic doctor uses it. Region | Position | Criterion | Quadriceps | Prone | Heel touches the buttock | Hamstrings | Supine, locked knee, leg raised with help | Leg above 70 degrees | Hip flexors | Hips at the table edge, one knee hugged | Suspended leg: knee below hip level | Shoulder | Standing or sitting, one hand over and one under | Good (fingers touch), average (small gap) or poor (large gap) | Sit and reach measures hamstring and lumbar flexibility. The box version reads the marker on the scale. The YMCA version needs a mat, a brown tape (1 foot, heel to heel) and a measuring tape whose 15 inch mark lies at the brown tape (the zero point). Case: male, 35 years, reaches 2 inches past the tape: 15 + 2 = 17 inches, which is Good (26-35 column). YMCA sit and reach layout

Using a norms chart Every chart is looked up by gender, age and the result. Only a standardised test gives a result that can be compared with the chart. A modified test gives a number that cannot be looked up. The lecture says the charts come from well-accepted research from several countries and are accepted globally.

Term | Meaning | Densitometry | Finding body fat from body density (mass / volume) | Archimedes principle | Displaced water volume equals the object volume, and equals the buoyant force | Buoyant force | Upward force on an object in water | Siri equation | Converts body density to body fat percentage | Gold standard | The most accurate reference test | DEXA | Dual energy X-ray absorptiometry | Validity | The test gives the body fat percentage | VO2 max | Maximal oxygen consumption (ml per kg per minute) | Maximal / sub-maximal test | Taken to the peak (athletes) or estimated from a lower effort (general clients) | Heart rate recovery | How quickly heart rate falls after activity | Standardised test | Every step, setting and condition fixed | Metronome | Device that ticks at set beats per minute | 1 RM | Heaviest weight lifted once with correct form and full range of motion | Relative strength | Weight lifted / body weight | Muscular endurance | Repeated contractions without fatigue (counted till failure) | Goniometer | Instrument that measures joint angle | Passive lengthening | Muscle lengthened with outside help (definition of flexibility used here) |

Part 1: the volume of the object underwater equals the volume of water displaced. Part 2: the water displaced equals the buoyant force on the object. Fat has more volume, displaces more water, has a higher buoyant force and is lighter than water. Muscle is the opposite on each point. Fat floats and muscle sinks. Air in the lungs makes a person float and would distort the underwater weight. The reading is taken when the bubbles stop. It gives the highest accuracy, and other tests are compared with it. It needs technical expertise, is expensive and is not available in India. Dual energy X-ray absorptiometry. Two X-ray beams are sent in, and denser tissue (bone) absorbs more than less dense tissue (fat). Fat-free mass, fat mass (including essential fat) and bone and mineral mass. Anthropometry is not valid (no body fat percentage). Skinfold is valid but not reliable (subcutaneous fat only). Hydrostatic weighing and the Bod Pod are not available in India. Of BIA and DEXA, DEXA gives the in-depth analysis and its accuracy is compared with the gold standard. Get a DEXA, compare it with the BIA reading (about plus or minus 5 percent), keep that margin in mind, and repeat DEXA after about 6 months. A maximal test takes the person to peak effort in a laboratory and is for athletes. A sub-maximal test estimates VO2 max from a lower effort and is for general clients. Time, pulse, age and weight in pounds. The pulse is counted for 10 seconds and multiplied by 6, immediately at the end. Weight 60 x 2.2 = 132 lbs. 139.168 - 19.400 - 10.164 - 48.975 - 16.848 = 43.781, which the slide prints as 43.79. This is Very good. 12 inches, 96 beats per minute, 3 minutes non-stop. One beat is one move (up, up, down, down). The Rockport test needs the peak heart rate, so a 10-second count is used. The step test measures recovery, so the full minute after exercise is counted. Excellent, because 85 is below 88 in the 26-35 female column. Relative strength = weight lifted / body weight (the strength ratio). The leg press is supported and does not depend on the core, but the squat is unsupported and depends on a strong core. Strength is skipped at the first test, the second test is the first strength test, and from the third test progress is tracked. Males use the toes and females use the knees. A full repetition has the chin touching the floor and the arms fully extended, with no half repetitions. The test is done till failure. 8 cm (over 45). Two beats make one repetition (one up, one down). The suspended leg is tested. It passes when the knee goes below the hip level. A mat, a 1 foot brown tape heel to heel, and a measuring tape whose 15 inch mark lies at the brown tape. The client keeps the knees straight and reaches forward. The result is 15 + 2 = 17 inches, which is Good.
